The question that matters — WHOSE plan_sections serves the writer path — is settled three ways, all 2026-08-10: (a) CONFIG: page-build-handler's call_content_writer input_mapping passes its section_plan output to the writer, whose check_section_plan keeps a caller-supplied plan VERBATIM ('Build the section plan the caller did not supply', bugs_open/087) — the writer's own plan_sections is the no-caller fallback; (b) LIVE: 30/30 page-content-writer orchestrations in the retained window (oldest 2026-08-09T18:06Z) carried a caller-supplied section_plan, 0 planned locally; (c) TRANSIT: the stamped fields survive the writer's pipeline — resolve_internal_links is a Go action that mutates section maps IN PLACE and returns the same slice (resolve_internal_links_action.go, return {'sections_ready': sections}), and select_sections' extract_fields copies whole entries. So 328 targets the RIGHT agent, on grounds that are now stated rather than assumed. Residual boundary, stated: a writer spawned with NO caller plan would build unscoped sections and fall to the site-wide branch — today's behaviour, and unobserved in the retained window.

(6) bug_historian MEDIUM, UPHELD and FIXED IN THIS RESUBMISSION — an object entry whose facts key is absent or malformed was skipped before pending, indistinguishable from a page correctly assigned no facts, which is exactly the disobedience seed 333's measurement depends on catching. carrySectionFactsOntoRealised now returns those names separately; they land in reconcileCounts.FactAssignmentAbsent and persist as FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT rows (distinct code, same agent_error_log channel as FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION). plan.summary: Wire the consumption half of plan-time fact assignment, and fix the reason it could not reach a built page. Consumption: page-build-handler passes each ready section's assigned facts to the writer (seed 328, opt-in step-config key), and writer prompt v4 branches on current_section.facts_scoped — scoped sections state ONLY their assigned facts, '[]' sections state none, unscoped sections keep today's site-wide block byte-identically (seed 330). Candidate 1b: carrySectionFactsOntoRealised re-attaches assignments onto a built page's restored composition by component name, misses recorded durably as FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION, and seed 362 shows the planner the realised section list so the match is near-total rather than coincidental. Seed 333 (planner: object form mandatory per page, owner decision RFC_016 s5.3) is included for review although already applied, so the round covers the full prompt breadth the guardian vetoed shipping unreviewed. RESUBMISSION: adds the upheld §3.5 fix (FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT), the two owner-ruled durable detections (RECOMPOSE_INTENT_NOT_REALISED, PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY), DO/RAISE ordering guards in 328/330, the corrected plan_sections census, and the discharged compliance read; drops applied seed 333 from edits.

edits.rationale: SHIPPED (f611dde6a, pod-verified on the current replicas): the carry, both loss sites, and the durable miss rows — original edits 1-2 and 4 of this correlation, unchanged in design. The carry itself. Matching is by component NAME because that is the only identity the two lists share: the realised list is plain strings, ordering and length differ, and a positional cross-reference that outlives the state it counted is the defect RFC_016 s1a names (and bugs_open/214 is living proof of, on the imagery wire). A name may repeat on a page — two text blocks — so assignments queue per name and the Nth realised entry of a name takes the Nth assignment, rather than all of them collapsing onto slot one. The result is emitted in the planner's OWN object form, so nothing new has to understand it: validate_plan's normalise pass splits it exactly as it splits the planner's own emission. When nothing carries, the realised slice is returned UNCHANGED — that is what keeps every pre-seed-333 plan byte-identical, and it is asserted, not assumed.

A correction, not a refinement, and the reviewers should weigh it as the most surprising thing in this round. The predicate compared whole entries with fmt.Sprintf("%v", ...). Once seed 333 made the planner emit OBJECTS against a realised list of plain STRINGS, %v of a map never equals %v of a string, so every composed page compared 'changed': snapped_sections silently stopped counting composition changes and started counting shape differences, and each one forced a restore over a list that was already identical. No Go changed to cause that — a row in agent_definitions did. Comparing by section name restores the counter's meaning and, as a side effect, makes the equal-composition case free: the planner's entries stay, so their assignments survive with no carry at all. Filed as a LANDMINE because the general form is that a live prompt edit can redefine a Go metric between two reads of it.

NEW, fixes the round's upheld bug_historian objection: an object entry whose facts key is absent/null/malformed was skipped before pending, so it never reached unmatched and never produced a durable row — invisible disobedience of seed 333's mandatory-facts rule, indistinguishable from a page correctly assigned no facts. The carry now returns those names as a fourth value; call sites append them to reconcileCounts.FactAssignmentAbsent; recordFactAssignmentAbsent persists FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT rows (distinct code, same channel and best-effort semantics as FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION). Boundary stated: fires only where the carry runs (Pass B/B2 restores); a page that compares EQUAL post-362 never reaches it — the emission-side detection for that case is site_plan_sections censuses, not this path.

edits.rationale: Candidate 1b (i). The planner was already GIVEN this data — existing_pages is an input_field of plan_site and load_existing_pages already selects p.sections — the prompt simply never printed it. So the planner could not know what a built page is composed of, re-composed it freely, and (since seed 333 made assignment mandatory per section) attached its assignments to names the built page does not have. The last sentence of the addition is deliberate and load-bearing: recompose_pages releases a page from the preservation guard and the planner is not told which pages those are, so an unconditional 'always re-emit' would silently defeat deliberate redesign. Anchors derived byte-exact from a fresh dump, never retyped.
edits.sketch:
{{range .existing_pages}}- name: {{.name}} | page_type: {{.page_type}} | url: {{.url}}
+{{if .sections}} | sections: {{.sections}}{{end}}

  ...Do not invent placeholder or example pages such as "post".
+ Each existing page is listed with the "sections:" it is actually built from. That composition is
+ preserved when the plan is validated, so for a page shown with a section list, re-emit that exact
+ list, in that order, as its "sections" array — do not re-compose it and do not substitute similar
+ component names. This matters for fact assignment (RULES, rule 17): an assignment travels inside
+ the section entry you emit, so a fact you attach to a section name this page does not have is
+ discarded silently. Put each carried-over page's fact assignments on the section names shown for
+ it. A page shown as "sections: []" is rendered by another part of the system — emit an empty
+ "sections" array for it and assign it no facts. Only when the briefing explicitly asks for a page
+ to be redesigned should you propose a different composition for it, and then its fact assignments
+ must name the NEW sections.

plan.risks:
THE ONE A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK FIRST — object form now exists in a window it did not before. The carry emits the planner's object form into pages["sections"] BETWEEN the reconcile (:3101) and the normalise pass (:3277). Everything downstream of validate_plan still sees plain strings, and the two loops inside that window read either shape via sectionEntryName. But that is a claim about a 176-line window in one function, and if the normalise pass were ever moved above the reconcile, or an early return were added between them, object form would escape into sync_pages_to_db and into pages.sections, whose every reader expects strings. The end-to-end test fails loudly if that happens; a reviewer who thinks a comment is insufficient protection here is not wrong, and the honest answer is that the test is the control, not the comment.

THE COUNTER CHANGED MEANING AND NO CODE DID IT. snapped_sections has been counting shape differences rather than composition changes since seed 333 shipped, because sameSectionList compared whole entries with %v. Any figure read across that boundary is two measurements with one name. This round corrects it; it does not retro-correct anything already recorded, and nothing in this lane's docs quotes such a figure. Filed as a LANDMINE, footprinted on the symbol, because the general form — a live prompt edit redefining a Go metric with no build — will recur on any counter whose predicate compares LLM output structurally.

THE PROMPT HALF INTERACTS WITH DELIBERATE REDESIGN. Seed 362 tells the planner to re-emit a built page's realised sections verbatim. recompose_pages exists precisely to redesign such a page, and it releases it from the preservation guard — but the planner is NOT told which pages are on that list, so the instruction carries an explicit escape ('only when the briefing explicitly asks for a page to be redesigned'). That escape is prose, and prose is a weaker control than a field. It is the strongest available without plumbing recompose_pages into the prompt, which is a bigger change than this round should carry; a reviewer who wants that plumbing should say so and it becomes a follow-up.

MISS RECORDS WILL APPEAR, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING. Once 362 applies, a FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION row means the planner disobeyed the re-emit instruction, not that the carry is broken. Before 362 applies, rows are expected and measure the structural gap. Do not read the row count as a defect rate without saying which side of 362 it was taken on.

THE CONSUMPTION FLIP, unchanged from the draft. It changes what the writer is TOLD on scoped sections only; the unscoped arm must remain byte-identical to today's behaviour — check the v4 template's else-branch reproduces the v3 writer_block injection exactly (the committed plaintext makes that a line diff). Rebuilds after apply rewrite scoped sections' prose: on fact-rich sites that is the intended effect (dedup), on fact-blind sites nothing changes (facts_scoped never set — their five census scores are the no-move control). A planner that disobeys rule 17 produces NULL assignments, which fall into the unscoped arm = today's behaviour, so disobedience fails SAFE.

APPLY ORDER MATTERS: 362, then 328, then 330 (a v4 prompt without the wiring key sees no facts_scoped and behaves as v3); all after the human read of the v4 plaintext. Known defect deliberately out of scope: imagery scope_ref orphans (bugs_open/214, filed with census and fix candidates) — same wire, different field; its fix does not gate this round. NEW SINCE THE REVISE: the three additions are observability-only — warning rows on agent_error_log, no change to any plan the validator or plan writer produces (their tests pin the no-op cases). RECOMPOSE_INTENT_NOT_REALISED cannot distinguish a dropped page from a renamed one (stated in the row's message); FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT covers only the carry path (Pass B/B2 restores) — a page comparing EQUAL post-362 is not scanned by it, so it measures disobedience on restored pages, not fleet-wide; PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY fires only in the composed-vs-composed branch that has never been observed live, which is exactly why it must be durable.
